title: A seven-dimensional hypersurface link
notes: The notebook intersects \(z_1^3+z_2^{3k-1}+z_3^2+z_4^2+z_5^2=0\) with \(\sum|z_i|^2=\epsilon\), and counts \(10-3=7\) real dimensions.
statement: For integers \(k\geq1\), the corrected Brieskorn link \(\Sigma(3,6k-1,2,2,2)\subset\mathbb C^5\), cut out on a sufficiently small positive sphere, is a smooth closed real seven-manifold and a homotopy sphere. The written exponent \(3k-1\) does not give homology spheres for every \(k\).
reconstruction: \(6k-1\) is our mathematical emendation. In the exponent graph for \((3,3k-1,2,2,2)\), odd \(k\) leaves an even component of four vertices, which fails the homology-sphere criterion. Even \(k=2\ell\) gives the standard family with parameter \(\ell\).
fate: Brieskorn published the construction in 1966; Hirzebruch explained its sphere criterion in his November 1966 expos\'e, printed in 1968 \citep[\S\S2--3]{brieskorn1966beispiele,hirzebruch1968singularities}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The notebook is an early report of an existing construction, with a substantive exponent error.

title: Twenty-eight oriented seven-sphere classes
notes: As \(k\) varies, all 28 “Milnor spheres” are said to occur.
statement: The group of oriented smooth homotopy seven-spheres is \(\Theta_7=bP_8\cong\mathbb Z/28\). With the corrected exponent, 28 consecutive parameters represent its 28 oriented diffeomorphism classes, including the standard sphere.
reconstruction: The orientation convention and inclusion of the standard sphere are supplied explicitly.
fate: The signature computation and the enumeration are given in \citet[\S3]{hirzebruch1968singularities}, reporting the 1966 construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; 28 counts all classes, not 28 exotic classes.

title: The analogous eleven-dimensional enumeration
notes: The report adds that the same method produces 992 spheres in dimension 11.
statement: Adding two quadratic variables gives \(\Sigma(3,6k-1,2,2,2,2,2)\), a homotopy eleven-sphere. Its classes exhaust \(\Theta_{11}=bP_{12}\cong\mathbb Z/992\), with orientations retained.
reconstruction: The explicit seven-variable polynomial is reconstructed from the phrase “the same method.”
fate: \citet[\S3]{hirzebruch1968singularities} gives the corresponding higher-dimensional signature calculation and the order 992.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. This numerical claim survives correction of the preceding family.

title: Local rigidity of the standard higher-rank lattice
notes: For \(n>2\), a continuous family of homomorphisms \(\varphi_t:\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\to\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)\) starting with inclusion has the form \(g(t)\gamma g(t)^{-1}\).
statement: For \(n\geq3\), the standard inclusion is locally rigid: all homomorphisms sufficiently close on a finite generating set are conjugate to it. A continuous parameter path starting at inclusion is locally conjugate; a path of conjugators can be chosen on an interval by lifting through the conjugation orbit.
reconstruction: Closeness on generators and the local-to-path interpretation are made explicit.
fate: \citet[\S16, Corollaries 16.4--16.5 and the following remark]{bassmilnorserre1967congruence} give the cohomological rigidity consequences; publication was in 1967 by Bass, Milnor and Serre, whose work Kazhdan is reporting.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. This is local deformation rigidity, not the assertion that arbitrary homomorphisms belong to one component.

title: The first-cohomology criterion
notes: The derivative of a deformation is a 1-cocycle with values in the adjoint module; conjugation produces a coboundary. Vanishing \(H^1\) is used to prove rigidity.
statement: For a finitely generated group \(\Gamma\), Lie group \(G\), and homomorphism \(\rho\), a differentiable path has infinitesimal class in \(H^1(\Gamma,\mathfrak g_{\operatorname{Ad}\rho})\). If that group vanishes, Weil’s local rigidity criterion applies. Nonzero cohomology alone need not integrate to a nontrivial deformation.
reconstruction: The warning about nonintegrable cocycles is an editorial clarification.
fate: The criterion predates this talk and is explicitly used in \citet[\S16, remark on rigidity]{bassmilnorserre1967congruence}; it recurs from 1964-8.2.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the obstruction to integrating arbitrary cocycles must not be omitted.

title: Passing from an integral adjoint lattice to real coefficients
notes: The notes choose \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb Z)\) and identify real first cohomology with its integral counterpart tensored with \(\mathbb R\).
statement: For a finitely presented \(\Gamma\) and a finite-rank free integral \(\Gamma\)-module \(L\), \(H^1(\Gamma,L)\otimes\mathbb R\cong H^1(\Gamma,L\otimes\mathbb R)\). Thus finiteness of the integral group proves real vanishing.
reconstruction: Finite presentation makes the cocycle relations a finite matrix calculation and justifies tensoring their kernels with the flat module \(\mathbb R\).
fate: The integral conclusion appears in \citet[Corollary 16.5]{bassmilnorserre1967congruence}; the change-of-scalars step is elementary homological algebra.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct with finiteness hypotheses. No assertion about all degrees or arbitrary coefficient modules is intended.

title: Reduction modulo a prime and the missing restriction term
notes: The proof attempts to make multiplication by \(p\) surjective on \(H^1(\Gamma,L)\), then reduces to a finite quotient and to \(H^1(\Gamma/\Gamma_p,L/pL)=0\).
statement: From \(0\to L\xrightarrow{p}L\to L/pL\to0\), vanishing \(H^1(\Gamma,L/pL)\) implies \(p\)-surjectivity. For finitely generated abelian \(H^1(\Gamma,L)\), this excludes a free summand. But inflation--restriction also has \(H^1(\Gamma_p,L/pL)^{\Gamma/\Gamma_p}\); vanishing on the quotient does not alone remove that term.
reconstruction: Our reconstruction supplies the exact-sequence obstruction and deliberately does not infer the missing vanishing.
fate: The final finiteness theorem matches \citet[Corollary 16.5]{bassmilnorserre1967congruence}, by the authors whose work is being reported; the exact prime-reduction proof in these notes was not matched to a complete published argument.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the conclusion is established; the recorded proof remains incomplete, rather than an independent open theorem.

title: A U-system is uniformly hyperbolic on the whole manifold
notes: The tangent bundle splits into \(X\oplus Y\), with one part contracted and the other expanded; such an automorphism is a \(U\)-system.
statement: A \(C^1\) diffeomorphism \(f\) of a closed smooth manifold is Anosov if \(TM=E^s\oplus E^u\) is a continuous invariant splitting and \(\|Df^nv^s\|,\|Df^{-n}v^u\|\leq C\lambda^n\|v^{s,u}\|\) for \(n\geq0\), \(C<\infty\), \(0<\lambda<1\).
reconstruction: The modern constants and bundle regularity explicate the shorthand.
fate: This is the established Anosov notion reviewed in \citet[\S\S1--2]{smale1967dynamical}; the survey followed the 1966 Moscow congress.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard. Continuity, invariance and uniform constants are essential.

title: Hyperbolic toral automorphisms
notes: A linear torus automorphism with no unit-modulus eigenvalues is the first example.
statement: If \(A\in\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb Z)\) has no eigenvalue of modulus one, \(x+\mathbb Z^d\mapsto Ax+\mathbb Z^d\) is Anosov. Its stable and unstable bundles descend from the generalized eigenspaces.
fate: The example is included in \citet[\S1]{smale1967dynamical}, and was already discussed in the earlier index at 1964-33.4.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established and explicit.

title: An arithmetic six-dimensional nilmanifold example
notes: Two real upper-unitriangular three-by-three groups are combined using the two embeddings of \(\mathbb Z[\sqrt3]\); the quotient is compact. No actual automorphism formula is retained.
statement: Let \(H\) have coordinates \((a,b,c)\) and law \((a,b,c)(a_2,b_2,c_2)=(a+a_2,b+b_2+ac_2,c+c_2)\). Embed \(H(\mathbb Z[\sqrt3])\) diagonally in \(H(\mathbb R)^2\) by conjugate embeddings. This is a uniform lattice. Multiplication of \(a,c\) by \(u=2+\sqrt3\) and of \(b\) by \(u^2\), with the conjugate action in the second factor, descends to an Anosov automorphism.
reconstruction: \ours\ The chosen map respects the cross-term because \((ua)(uc_2)=u^2ac_2\), preserves the integral lattice since \(u\) is a unit, and has eigenvalues \(u,u,u^2,u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-2}\). Compactness follows by reduction in the two-dimensional Minkowski lattice successively in \(a,c,b\).
fate: The nilmanifold family is part of the algebraic examples reviewed by \citet[\S1]{smale1967dynamical}; the formula supplied here is a compatible reconstruction, not a claimed verbatim match.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established construction; the scan determines the lattice more clearly than the missing map.

title: Are all Anosov examples algebraic?
notes: After the nilmanifold construction the notes suggest that all such systems may be of this kind.
statement: A precise modern version asks whether every Anosov diffeomorphism of a closed connected manifold is topologically conjugate to an affine Anosov automorphism of an infranilmanifold. The weaker manifold question asks only whether the manifold is homeomorphic to an infranilmanifold.
reconstruction: Topological conjugacy and infranilmanifolds are modern precisifications, not words legible in the notebook.
fate: The strong topological-conjugacy formulation is explicit in \citet[Conjecture 2.3]{spatzier2016rigidity}; \citet[Introduction]{deremainkar2023anosov} retain the weaker manifold question. The latter circulated in 2020, appeared online in 2022, and in print in 2023.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: no general resolution was found in the dated primary-source search. Smooth conjugacy and diffeomorphism to a standard smooth infranilmanifold are stronger, generally invalid replacements.
worth: Further work is worthwhile in a specified algebraic or dimension-restricted class; the unrestricted classification has no plausible bounded proof from these notes.

title: Structural stability and the choice of equivalence
notes: Nearby systems should be equivalent, initially described as diffeomorphic and subsequently as related by an \(\epsilon\)-homeomorphism.
statement: A diffeomorphism is \(C^r\) structurally stable if all sufficiently \(C^r\)-close diffeomorphisms are topologically conjugate. For vector fields use an orbit homeomorphism preserving time orientation, usually allowing reparameterization. A near-identity conjugacy is available in the hyperbolic stability setting.
reconstruction: The precise topology and the flow time-change convention are supplied.
fate: \citet[Introduction and \S2]{smale1967dynamical} uses topological equivalence. The same distinction is relevant to 1965-74.1.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; smooth conjugacy would wrongly preserve eigenvalue data under perturbation.

title: The two-dimensional structural-stability model
notes: Andronov--Pontryagin theory is cited as the two-dimensional precedent.
statement: For flows on a closed orientable surface, the classical criterion requires finitely many hyperbolic equilibria and periodic orbits, no saddle connections, and no other nonwandering recurrence. Such fields are structurally stable; the relevant density theorem is a \(C^1\) surface theorem.
reconstruction: The compact-surface formulation combines the precedent with the standard complete criterion; it is not attributed entirely to the original planar theorem.
fate: The historical surface theory and Peixoto’s extension are reviewed by \citet[\S2]{smale1967dynamical}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The notes do not justify transferring the density conclusion to higher dimensions.

title: Morse--Smale systems
notes: Finitely many hyperbolic stationary and periodic trajectories, convergence toward them, and transverse stable/unstable intersections are listed.
statement: For a smooth flow on a closed manifold, the nonwandering set must be a finite union of hyperbolic equilibria and periodic orbits, and their stable and unstable manifolds must meet transversely. For diffeomorphisms the nonwandering set consists of finitely many hyperbolic periodic points with the same transversality condition.
reconstruction: The nonwandering-set condition makes the informal convergence clause precise.
fate: The finite-hyperbolic/transverse formulation is the setting of \citet[Theorem 1.2 and \S5]{palissmale1970stability}, circulated in 1968.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; this definition is much narrower than Axiom A.

title: Does Morse--Smale imply structural stability?
notes: The heading says four assertions. Only the first, that Morse--Smale conditions imply stability, is explicitly marked as a question.
statement: Is every Morse--Smale diffeomorphism or flow on a closed manifold structurally stable in the \(C^1\) topology?
fate: Yes: \citet[Theorem 1.2; flow version in \S5]{palissmale1970stability}. The paper circulated in 1968, appeared in Russian in 1969, and in the cited proceedings in 1970.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: solved affirmatively.

title: Must a structurally stable system be Morse--Smale?
notes: The second assertion reverses the implication. The notebook groups assertions 2--4 under \ru{Опровергнуты Смейлом}: refuted by Smale.
statement: Does structural stability force only finitely many hyperbolic recurrent critical elements?
fate: The Anosov examples already refute this: see \citet[\S1]{smale1967dynamical}. A hyperbolic toral automorphism is structurally stable and has infinitely many periodic orbits; its suspension gives the flow analogue.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: false in general, with examples available in the theory discussed at the talk.

title: Are Morse--Smale systems dense?
notes: The third assertion proposes density of Morse--Smale systems; the notebook explicitly includes it among the three assertions refuted by Smale.
statement: Are Morse--Smale systems dense among all smooth systems on each closed manifold in a specified \(C^r\) topology?
fate: An open Anosov neighbourhood with infinitely many periodic orbits prevents this general density statement \citep[\S1]{smale1967dynamical}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: false in general; manifold- and dimension-specific density results do not repair the universal assertion.

title: Are structurally stable systems dense?
notes: The fourth assertion proposes density of structurally stable systems; the notebook already reports Smale’s refutation.
statement: Is the set of structurally stable \(C^r\) vector fields dense on every compact smooth manifold?
fate: \citet[Main theorem]{smale1966nondensity}, received in June 1965 and published in 1966, constructs a compact four-manifold with an open set containing no structurally stable fields.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: false in general. The negative result was already published and reported at this seminar.

title: A hyperbolic invariant set
notes: Uniform hyperbolicity is imposed on a closed invariant set, with a point, the whole space, and a Cantor-type set as examples.
statement: For a diffeomorphism, a compact invariant set \(\Lambda\) is hyperbolic when \(T_\Lambda M\) admits a continuous invariant stable/unstable splitting with uniform exponential estimates. For nonsingular flows add the one-dimensional flow direction. A horseshoe illustrates a proper, totally disconnected hyperbolic set.
reconstruction: The distinction between maps and flows is supplied.
fate: These examples and the invariant-set formulation appear in \citet[\S\S1--2]{smale1967dynamical}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; the flow-direction summand cannot be omitted from the flow definition.

title: Nonwandering points and Axiom A
notes: The nonwandering set \(\Omega\) is closed; “Smale systems” satisfy hyperbolicity of \(\Omega\) and density in it of periodic points.
statement: For a homeomorphism of a compact space, \(x\in\Omega(f)\) if every neighbourhood \(U\) meets \(f^nU\) for some \(n>0\). A \(C^1\) diffeomorphism satisfies Axiom A when \(\Omega(f)\) is hyperbolic and \(\overline{\operatorname{Per}(f)}=\Omega(f)\).
reconstruction: The modern name Axiom A is used retrospectively.
fate: The two independent clauses are those used by \citet[\S\S2--3]{smale1967dynamical}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard. On a flow, equilibria must also be included among the recurrent critical elements.

title: Nonwandering does not imply periodic
notes: The discussion mentions a system with every point nonwandering but no periodic trajectories.
statement: An irrational rotation \(x\mapsto x+\alpha\) of \(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\), \(\alpha\notin\mathbb Q\), has \(\Omega=S^1\) and no periodic point. This example is not hyperbolic.
reconstruction: The irrational rotation is our explicit model for the brief example.
fate: This elementary distinction is consistent with the separate hypotheses in \citet[\S2]{smale1967dynamical}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established counterexample to a claim without hyperbolicity.

title: Generic density of periodic points in the nonwandering set
notes: A generic periodic-point density theorem is attributed to a difficult-to-read name with a 1964 date.
statement: For a residual subset of \(\operatorname{Diff}^1(M)\) of a closed smooth manifold, \(\Omega(f)=\overline{\operatorname{Per}(f)}\). The analogous generic flow statement includes equilibria. This is a \(C^1\), not an unrestricted \(C^r\), conclusion.
fate: \citet[Theorem 6.5 in the Russian version]{pugh1967density}, published in 1967, states the generic flow result; the diffeomorphism formulation above is its standard counterpart. The paper refers to earlier announcements, but the handwritten name/date remains insecure.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in \(C^1\). The ambiguous marginal attribution is retained as ambiguous.

title: Density of Axiom A systems
notes: A conjecture asks whether systems satisfying the two Smale conditions are dense.
statement: Are Axiom A diffeomorphisms \(C^1\)-dense on every closed smooth manifold?
fate: The general conjecture failed through the robust examples of \citet{abrahamsmale1970nongenericity}; this is a different assertion from Smale’s earlier nondensity of structural stability.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: false in general. Density in restricted classes is a separate question.

title: Does hyperbolicity of the nonwandering set imply dense periodic points?
notes: The possibility that condition 1 implies condition 2 is assigned “70\%” confidence.
statement: If the nonwandering set of a smooth diffeomorphism of a compact manifold is hyperbolic, must periodic points be dense in that set?
fate: No: \citet[main counterexample]{kurata1979hyperbolic} constructs a hyperbolic nonwandering set without dense periodic points.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: refuted in general. Local maximality and shadowing cannot be silently supplied to the arbitrary nonwandering set.

title: Spectral decomposition into basic sets
notes: The nonwandering set decomposes into finitely many invariant transitive pieces.
statement: For an Axiom A diffeomorphism on a closed manifold, \(\Omega(f)\) is a disjoint union of finitely many compact invariant topologically transitive basic sets. Periodic density belongs among the hypotheses, even if a preceding speculative implication would have removed it.
reconstruction: Axiom A is stated explicitly rather than inferred from condition 1.
fate: The spectral decomposition theorem is given in \citet[\S3]{smale1967dynamical}, published in 1967. The notebook attests its circulation here in September 1966; an independently checked earlier public-circulation date for this exact statement is not asserted.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established under Axiom A. The two-clause assumption matters because the preceding conjecture is false.

title: The regular uniform algebra on a Hilbert ball
notes: For the unit ball \(S\subset H\), \(L(S)\subset\overline R\subset C(S)\), where \(R\) consists of continuous functions of finitely many coordinates and distances \(\|x-a_j\|\).
statement: Let \(H\) be an infinite-dimensional separable real Hilbert space. In the supremum norm on its closed unit ball, let \(A\) be the uniform closure of the unital algebra generated by the linear coordinates and \(\|x\|^2\). This equals the stated coordinate-and-distance algebra. One has \(C(S_{\rm weak})\subset A\subset C_b(S_{\rm norm})\).
reconstruction: The identity \(\|x-a\|^2=\|x\|^2-2\langle x,a\rangle+\|a\|^2\) explains the equivalent generators. The subscript \(b\) is an explicit clarification.
fate: The regular algebra is defined in \citet[\S1]{shilov1967hilbert1}, received 4 January 1967.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The ambient norm-continuous algebra must be bounded if a uniform Banach-algebra norm is intended.

title: A compactification and its nonevaluation characters
notes: The maximal-ideal space of \(L(S)\) is the Hilbert ball; that of \(\overline R\) is a compact extension.
statement: The character space of \(C(S_{\rm weak})\) is the weakly compact ball. For \(A\), an explicit model is \(K=\{(z,s):\|z\|^2\leq s\leq1\}\subset S_{\rm weak}\times[0,1]\), with evaluation points \((x,\|x\|^2)\). Points with \(s>\|z\|^2\) are additional characters.
reconstruction: \ours\ The set \(K\) is compact because norm squared is weakly lower semicontinuous. The generators extend continuously and separate its points. Evaluation points are dense: use \(x_j=z+\sqrt{s-\|z\|^2}\,e_j\), with orthonormal \(e_j\perp z\). Stone--Weierstrass then identifies \(A\) with \(C(K)\).
fate: \citet[\S1 and the reference to Part II]{shilov1967hilbert1} connects the regular algebra to its maximal ideals. The concrete model here is supplied as a reconstruction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the compactification is well defined; it is not the norm ball itself.

title: Limiting spherical and ball means coincide
notes: Finite-dimensional means on spheres and balls have the same infinite-dimensional limit on \(\overline R\).
statement: For admissible centres \(z\) and radii \(r\), normalized means over increasing finite-dimensional balls or spheres converge for every \(f\in A\), independently of the orthonormal exhaustion. On a generator \(F(\langle e_1,x\rangle,\ldots,\langle e_m,x\rangle,\|x\|^2)\), the limit is \(F(\langle e_1,z\rangle,\ldots,\langle e_m,z\rangle,\|z\|^2+r^2)\).
reconstruction: The displayed formula spells out the finite-coordinate concentration calculation; admissibility means the averaging sets lie in the domain.
fate: The mean construction is in \citet[\S2]{shilov1967hilbert1}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established on this algebra; it is not a countably additive uniform measure on an infinite-dimensional sphere.

title: The mean is multiplicative
notes: \(M_r\) is a multiplicative functional, usually evaluation only in the compact extension.
statement: For \(f,g\in A\), \(M_r(fg,z)=M_r(f,z)M_r(g,z)\). For \(r>0\) this is evaluation at \((z,\|z\|^2+r^2)\in K\), not at a Hilbert-space point.
fate: \citet[\S2]{shilov1967hilbert1} establishes multiplicativity.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; finite-dimensional averaging is not multiplicative, and the limiting assertion relies on the restricted regular algebra.

title: The mean-defined first-order derivation
notes: \(\Delta f(z)=\lim_{r\to0}[M_r(f,z)-f(z)]/r^2\), with the emphatic comment that it is first order and obeys Leibniz’s rule.
statement: On the domain where this limit exists in the stipulated topology, the mean generator \(L\) is a derivation: \(L(fg)=fLg+gLf\). On smooth regular functions expressed in \((z,s)\), it differentiates in the \(s\)-direction at \(s=\|z\|^2\). In particular \(L\|x\|^2=1\), while it annihilates a smooth finite-coordinate function.
reconstruction: The notation \(L\) avoids confusion with a trace Laplacian. The examples follow directly from the notebook’s normalization.
fate: The operator and its derivation property are in \citet[\S\S2,5]{shilov1967hilbert1}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established for its specified function class and closure. It should not be identified with the ordinary sum of second derivatives.

title: A regular Dirichlet problem
notes: For a star-shaped surface \(\sum_{k>m}\xi_k^2=\varphi(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m)\) with bounded curvature, the Dirichlet problem has a unique, continuously dependent solution given by an angular mean.
statement: In Shilov’s regular boundary class, the mean-defined operator has a unique regular harmonic extension of regular continuous boundary data, with continuous dependence in the uniform norm. An unqualified assertion for every weakly closed star-shaped surface is not supported. Even the norm unit sphere is not weakly closed in infinite dimension.
reconstruction: The scope is restricted to the published regular-domain construction instead of guessing a general geometric theorem from “bounded curvature.”
fate: The linear boundary construction and uniqueness are in \citet[\S\S3,6]{shilov1967hilbert1}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the published regular-domain framework; the notebook does not retain all the domain hypotheses.

title: A Poisson inverse for the regular operator
notes: The inhomogeneous problem \(\Delta u=g\in\overline R\) also has an explicit formula.
statement: For the same regular boundary problem, separate a harmonic extension of the boundary data and a zero-boundary solution operator \(P\) satisfying \(LPg=g\) on the allowed regular class. Boundedness of \(P\), with the relevant domain norm, is needed for continuous dependence.
reconstruction: The operator notation \(P\) is introduced for the next fixed-point step.
fate: \citet[\S\S4--5]{shilov1967hilbert1} gives the inhomogeneous construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established within that framework.

title: Semilinear equations by a fixed point
notes: \(\Delta u=\varphi(x,u(x))\) is said to be solved by a fixed-point method.
statement: A sufficient abstract version is: on a closed ball of the regular Banach function space, \(T(u)=h+P\varphi(\cdot,u)\) preserves the ball and \(\varphi\) is uniformly Lipschitz in \(u\) with \(\|P\|\operatorname{Lip}_u\varphi<1\). Then \(T\) has a unique fixed point, solving the specified boundary problem.
reconstruction: The ball-invariance and contraction assumptions are our transparent sufficient version, not a claim that they reproduce the strongest published theorem.
fate: The nonlinear programme was published in \citet[Theorems 1--2]{shilov1967hilbert3}, received 16 February 1967.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established under appropriate existence hypotheses. The bare phrase does not prove global solvability for arbitrary nonlinearities.

title: Hyperbolicity requires more than a real spectrum
notes: \(u_t=A(u)u_x\) is called hyperbolic when all eigenvalues of \(A(u)\) are real.
statement: For a standard one-dimensional strictly hyperbolic quasilinear system, \(A\) is smooth on an open state set and has \(n\) distinct real eigenvalues there. For non-strict notions, diagonalizability and uniform control of eigenvectors must be specified; a real spectrum alone allows defective matrices.
reconstruction: Strict hyperbolicity is a sufficient precise scope, not an assertion that every physical example has distinct speeds.
fate: The modern strict-hyperbolicity setting of \citet[Theorem 1]{bianchinibressan2005viscosity} makes the assumptions needed for the later uniqueness question explicit.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the notebook’s definition is incomplete for standard well-posedness theorems.

title: Scalar convexity does not select a unique weak solution
notes: For \(n=1\), uniqueness is said always to hold when \(f\) is convex.
statement: For \(u_t+F(u)_x=0\) with smooth scalar flux and bounded initial data, entropy admissibility yields the standard unique solution. Convexity alone does not make arbitrary distributional solutions unique. For Burgers flux \(F(u)=u^2/2\) and data 0 left, 1 right, both an expansion shock of speed \(1/2\) and the rarefaction fan are weak solutions.
reconstruction: \ours\ The shock satisfies Rankine--Hugoniot since \((1/2-0)/(1-0)=1/2\). The fan is \(u=0,x\leq0\), \(u=x/t,0<x<t\), \(u=1,x\geq t\); it solves the equation in each region and is continuous across its interfaces. Their common initial trace proves nonuniqueness without admissibility.
fate: Entropy selection was present in \citet{oleinik1957discontinuous}; the general scalar uniqueness framework is \citet{kruzhkov1970first}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal weak-solution claim is false; the entropy formulation is established.

title: Hydrodynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, and an unspecified Godunov class
notes: Two-component hydrodynamics and apparently magnetohydrodynamics are said to have uniqueness; a narrow class treated by Godunov is mentioned.
statement: No single uniqueness theorem can be recovered without the exact equations, state restrictions, domain, data, and admissibility criterion. These fragments do not establish uniqueness for every Euler or magnetohydrodynamic system.
fate: The checked scalar and strictly hyperbolic literature does not identify these particular fragments: \citet{oleinik1957discontinuous,bianchinibressan2005viscosity} are comparisons only.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: unidentified at theorem level; not evidence of an undeveloped problem.

title: Convexity along an eigenvector field
notes: Draw eigenvectors in state space; convexity may mean growth of the corresponding eigenvalue along their integral curves.
statement: If \(A(u)r_i(u)=\lambda_i(u)r_i(u)\) is a smooth simple eigenpair, the genuine-nonlinearity condition is \(D\lambda_i(u)\cdot r_i(u)\ne0\). Linear degeneracy means that derivative vanishes identically. These are properties of characteristic fields in state space, distinct from the space-time characteristics of one solution.
reconstruction: The derivative condition and distinction of the two kinds of curves are supplied.
fate: This is the classical characteristic-field distinction from Lax’s 1957 theory, discussed in the historical setup of \citet{bianchinibressan2005viscosity}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the notebook gives the correct geometric idea without specifying nonvanishing or normalization.

title: Conservation form and the meaning of a shock
notes: Writing \(u_t=\partial_x f(u)\) is said to be better than general quasilinear form.
statement: For a conservative system \(u_t+F(u)_x=0\), weak solutions and jump conditions are defined distributionally. For a general nonconservative matrix \(A(u)\), \(A(u)u_x\) is not canonically defined at jumps; a regularization or prescribed nonconservative product is additional data.
reconstruction: The distributional explanation is supplied.
fate: The conservative/nonconservative distinction is explicit in \citet[Introduction and Theorem 1]{bianchinibressan2005viscosity}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; the notebook’s plus-sign convention is converted by \(F=-f\).

title: Uniqueness selected by identity viscosity
notes: When does adding \(\epsilon u_{xx}\) give uniqueness?
statement: A definite interpretation asks whether, for smooth strictly hyperbolic \(A\) and common initial data, solutions of \(u_t+A(u)u_x=\epsilon u_{xx}\) converge as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) to one limit independent of subsequence. Small total variation, values in a fixed hyperbolicity neighbourhood, and the identity viscosity matrix specify an established scope.
reconstruction: The vanishing-viscosity interpretation is distinguished from the easier uniqueness of a fixed strictly parabolic equation.
fate: \citet[Theorem 1]{bianchinibressan2005viscosity} prove this small-BV statement, with uniform BV and Lipschitz dependence; the preprint circulated in November 2001 and publication followed in 2005.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: solved in the stated small-BV setting. The unrestricted wording does not specify a single larger well-posedness problem and is not claimed solved.

title: Travelling-wave reduction is local information
notes: The viscosity question is said to reduce to ordinary differential equations.
statement: For a conservative viscous system, a travelling profile \(U((x-st)/\epsilon)\) satisfies \(U^{\prime}=F(U)-F(u_-)-s(U-u_-)\) after integration, with end states at equilibria. For the notebook sign convention in a nonconservative system, the second-order equation is \(U^{\prime\prime}=-(A(U)+sI)U^{\prime}\).
reconstruction: \ours\ Both ODEs are derived here by substitution. They reconstruct a plausible local meaning of the last sentence, not the cancelled word.
fate: Travelling profiles are part of the analysis in \citet{bianchinibressan2005viscosity}; a full Cauchy-problem uniqueness proof needs substantially more.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the profile reduction is valid; equivalence to global uniqueness of arbitrary solutions is false.

title: The representation ring and associated universal bundles
notes: \(R_G\) is the commutative ring of finite-dimensional representations and their formal differences; a representation gives a bundle over \(B_G\).
statement: For compact Lie \(G\), use finite-dimensional complex continuous representations. Direct sum and tensor product define \(R(G)\). The associated-bundle construction sends \([V]\) to \([EG\times_GV]\in K^0(BG)\) and is a ring homomorphism.
fate: This construction underlies \citet[Introduction]{atiyahsegal1969completion}, whose introduction traces the finite-group and connected-group cases to 1961.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; complex coefficients and virtual bundles are made explicit.

title: The uncompleted map need not be an embedding
notes: The arrow \(R_G\to K(B_G)\) is labelled \ru{Вложение}.
statement: The map need not be injective for disconnected compact groups. In \(R(C_6)=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^6-1)\), let \(a=(x-1)(x+1)(x^2+x+1)\ne0\). Then \((x^2-x+1)a=0\) and \((x-1)(-x)a=a\), so \(a\in\bigcap_{n\geq1}(x-1)^nR(C_6)\); its completion image vanishes.
reconstruction: \ours\ The displayed polynomial has degree four and is nonzero modulo the monic degree-six relation. Since \(1+(x-1)x=x^2-x+1\), multiplication by \(-x\) is an inverse to \(x-1\) on the submodule generated by \(a\). Iteration proves membership in every augmentation power. The completion theorem then identifies its image in \(K^0(BC_6)\) with zero.
fate: The correct general statement is completion, as in \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}; the elementary cyclic-group calculation here checks the stronger notebook wording.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal embedding assertion is false in this generality.

title: Augmentation completion gives K of the classifying space
notes: Completing \(R_G\) at virtual representations of dimension zero gives \(K(B_G)\).
statement: For compact Lie \(G\), \(I_G=\ker(\dim:R(G)\to\mathbb Z)\) and \(\widehat{R(G)}_{I_G}=\varprojlim R(G)/I_G^n\). The associated-bundle map induces \(\widehat{R(G)}_{I_G}\cong K^0(BG)\); also \(K^1(BG)=0\).
fate: \citet[Introduction]{atiyahsegal1969completion} records the 1961 cases and supplies a unified 1969 proof; the seminar itself documents prior circulation of the general statement.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. Class E describes Bernstein’s explicit exposition of Atiyah, rather than a claim of a 1966 Bernstein discovery.

title: The circle completion is a formal power-series ring
notes: \(R_{S^1}=\sum n_ix^i\), only finitely many nonzero coefficients; \(y=x-1\) generates the augmentation ideal and \(\widehat R_{S^1}=\mathbb Z[[y]]\).
statement: \(R(S^1)=\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]\), where \(x\) is the weight-one character. Modulo \(y^n\), \(x=1+y\) is invertible; inverse limits therefore give \(\mathbb Z[[y]]\). The notebook’s geometric series \(1/(1-y)\) is an example of a formal series, not the expansion of \(x^{-1}\).
reconstruction: The inverse-limit justification and distinction of the two inverses are supplied.
fate: This is the standard circle example of the completion theorem \citep{atiyahsegal1969completion}; Atiyah’s course circulated in 1964 and appeared as \citet{atiyah1967ktheory}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established elementary calculation.

title: Projective space and its tautological line bundle
notes: \(B_{S^1}=\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}\); on \(\mathbb{CP}^n\) the canonical bundle is described as having fibre \(\mathbb{CP}^1\) and total space \(\mathbb{CP}^{n+1}\).
statement: The tautological complex line bundle \(L\to\mathbb{CP}^n\) has fibre the line \(\ell\cong\mathbb C\) above \([\ell]\). Its unit-circle bundle is \(S^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n\), with fibre \(S^1\). Neither the line bundle nor this circle bundle has total space \(\mathbb{CP}^{n+1}\).
reconstruction: The two actual bundles are distinguished to avoid guessing an unstated projectivization.
fate: The standard construction is part of Atiyah’s 1964 course, published as \citet{atiyah1967ktheory}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the model for \(BS^1\) is correct; the finite-dimensional bundle description is false as written.

title: K of finite and infinite complex projective space
notes: Every class on \(\mathbb{CP}^n\) is a polynomial in \(x-1\), and \((x-1)^{n+1}=0\); passage to the limit gives the infinite case.
statement: For \(x=[L]\), \(K^0(\mathbb{CP}^n)=\mathbb Z[x]/((x-1)^{n+1})\), \(K^1(\mathbb{CP}^n)=0\), and the compatible inverse limit is \(K^0(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})=\mathbb Z[[x-1]]\).
reconstruction: The odd K group is supplied to justify the uncomplicated inverse limit.
fate: This is the projective-space calculation in \citet{atiyah1967ktheory}, based on the 1964 lectures.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The exponent depends on the finite stage \(n\).

title: Skeletal inverse limits
notes: Take \(K((BG)_1)\leftarrow K((BG)_2)\leftarrow\cdots\) and its projective limit.
statement: For this completion problem, skeletal K-groups determine the completed theory. For a general countable CW filtration \(X=\bigcup X_n\), however, the comparison is governed by \(0\to\varprojlim{}^1K^{-1}(X_n)\to K^0(X)\to\varprojlim K^0(X_n)\to0\). The derived-limit term must be shown to vanish or the pro-system formulation retained.
reconstruction: The derived-limit caveat is supplied to prevent an overgeneralization.
fate: The filtration/completion distinction is explicit in \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}; the simple projective-space tower has vanishing odd groups.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: valid in the appropriate completed interpretation, not an unconditional definition of topological K-theory for every infinite complex.

title: Gelfand’s noncompact completion programme
notes: Generalize the K-functor and classifying space to locally compact Lie groups, using infinite-dimensional representations, so that the theorem remains valid.
statement: This specifies a programme but not a single theorem: it leaves the representation category, Grothendieck construction, completion ideal, and space unspecified. One precise later analogue treats finite proper \(G\)-CW complexes for discrete \(G\); this does not settle all locally compact Lie groups in one canonical interpretation.
fate: \citet[Theorems 3.2 and 4.3; \S5]{luckoliver2001completion} provide a proper-action analogue and explain difficulties for positive-dimensional noncompact groups.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: partly realized through several inequivalent theories, with no exact notebook conjecture to classify as solved or still open.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: A Plancherel factor in place of dimension
notes: Dimension is compared with an uncertain “factor” in the Plancherel formula.
statement: For a noncompact group, an irreducible unitary representation may be infinite-dimensional; formal degree or Plancherel density can play an analogue of dimension in some formulas. The fragment does not specify a multiplication law, an augmentation homomorphism, or even a class of representations.
fate: The noncompact K-theory comparison in \citet[\S5]{luckoliver2001completion} does not identify this particular suggestion. No exact theorem match was found.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: unidentifiable beyond the heuristic analogy.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Equivariant K-theory of vector bundles
notes: A \(G\)-bundle is a vector bundle with compatible linear action on fibres; take sums, tensor products, and formal differences. At a point the answer is \(R_G\).
statement: For compact Lie \(G\) acting on compact \(X\), \(K_G^0(X)\) is the Grothendieck group of finite-rank complex \(G\)-equivariant vector bundles. Fibre maps are linear and cover the given base action. Pullback from a point makes it an \(R(G)\)-module, and \(K_G^0(*)=R(G)\).
fate: The construction was already being taught by Atiyah; \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion} uses the theory systematically.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard for compact groups. Noncompact groups require additional qualifications.

title: The Borel construction
notes: \(X_G=E\times_GX\), with \(E\) a free right \(G\)-space over \(B_G\); for a point one recovers \(B_G\).
statement: Choose a contractible free right \(G\)-space \(EG\). For a left \(G\)-space \(X\), set \(X_G=(EG\times X)/((eg,x)\sim(e,gx))\). An equivariant bundle induces a bundle over \(X_G\), producing \(K_G^*(X)\to K^*(X_G)\).
reconstruction: Contractibility and the explicit quotient convention are supplied.
fate: This is the comparison map of \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; contractibility is required of the universal free space.

title: The equivariant completion theorem
notes: \(\widehat K_G(X)\cong K(X_G)\), with completion in the dimension-zero ideal of \(R_G\).
statement: For compact Lie \(G\) and a finite \(G\)-CW complex \(X\), completion at \(I_G\) gives \(\widehat{K_G^*(X)}_{I_G}\cong K^*(EG\times_GX)\). A pro-system version handles the filtration explicitly; a statement for an arbitrary \(G\)-space without finiteness assumptions is too broad.
reconstruction: The finite \(G\)-CW hypothesis is a safe standard formulation of the announced result.
fate: \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion} is the exact general theorem publication. The notebook proves its circulation through Atiyah by September 1966.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated finite equivariant-CW setting.

title: Completion by tensoring with the completed coefficient ring
notes: \(\widehat K_G(X)=K_G(X)\otimes_{R_G}\widehat R_G\) is offered as an exact definition.
statement: For a Noetherian ring \(R\), ideal \(I\), and finitely generated \(R\)-module \(M\), \(\widehat M_I\cong M\otimes_R\widehat R_I\). Here compact Lie \(G\) and a finite \(G\)-CW complex ensure the relevant finiteness. This tensor formula is not a universal definition for arbitrary modules.
reconstruction: The commutative-algebra hypotheses are supplied.
fate: This algebra is used in \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct with finite-generation assumptions.

title: Induction to a unitary group
notes: For \(G\subset U\), \(K_G(X)=K_U(U\times_GX)\), and \(X_G=(U\times_GX)_U\).
statement: For a closed inclusion of compact Lie groups \(G\subset U(N)\), induction gives an equivalence of equivariant vector-bundle categories over \(X\) and \(U(N)\times_GX\), hence the K-theory isomorphism. The corresponding Borel constructions are naturally equivalent using a common universal free \(U(N)\)-space.
reconstruction: Closed inclusion and common universal models make the displayed identities precise.
fate: This induction mechanism belongs to the completion proof in \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the equality of classifying constructions should be interpreted with the chosen models.

title: Maximal-torus splitting by a family index
notes: For a maximal torus \(T\subset U\), restriction embeds a direct summand, with a dashed reverse map to be explained analytically.
statement: For \(U=U(N)\), the flag manifold \(U/T\) is complex. The fibrewise Dolbeault index along \(U\times_TX\to X\) defines a retraction of restriction \(K_U(X)\to K_T(X)\): the projection formula and \(\operatorname{ind}_{U}(\bar\partial_{U/T})=1\) give \(p_!p^*=1\). The same mechanism compares the completed/Borel diagram.
reconstruction: The Dolbeault operator is our precise realization of the dashed arrow; the notebook postpones its definition to the family-index discussion.
fate: The direct-image strategy is discussed by Atiyah in \citet{atiyah1988commentary}; the theorem is \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. An arbitrary elliptic operator, or the de Rham Euler index, need not give 1.

title: Classical phase space and a Hamiltonian
notes: A physical system is a state space and a real Hamiltonian; the classical states are \((p_1,\ldots,p_N,x_1,\ldots,x_N)\), with \(p_i\in\mathbb R^\nu\), \(x_i\in\Omega\).
statement: For bounded measurable \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\), the labelled phase space is \(\mathbb R^{dN}\times\Omega^N\), possibly restricted by \(|x_i-x_j|>\delta\). With \(m>0\), \(H=\sum_i|p_i|^2/(2m)+W_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\). Forbidden configurations may equivalently have \(H=+\infty\).
reconstruction: Measurability and labelled-particle convention are explicit.
fate: Expository model setup: \citet[Lecture I]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; allowing \(+\infty\) reconciles hard cores with the earlier phrase real-valued.

title: Ordered pair interactions and identical systems
notes: \(W_N=\sum_{i\ne j}U(|x_i-x_j|)\); systems with fixed potential and mass but different \(N,\Omega\) are identical.
statement: The notebook sums over ordered distinct pairs. Thus \(\sum_{i\ne j}U=\sum_{i<j}\phi\) with the usual unordered pair potential \(\phi=2U\). A thermodynamic sequence fixes \(U,m,\beta\) while changing \(N\) and the vessel.
reconstruction: The conversion \(\phi=2U\) prevents silently importing a different normalization.
fate: The conventions are compared with \citet[Lecture I]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: consistent if the factor two is retained throughout; it is not a transcription error.

title: Integrating out momenta
notes: The configurational system omits kinetic energy; the full Gibbs density factors into momentum and position distributions.
statement: For \(\beta,m>0\), Gaussian integration contributes \((2\pi m/\beta)^{dN/2}\). The position marginal is \(Z_{N,\Omega}^{-1}e^{-\beta W_N}\), independently of the momentum variables. A fixed \(N!\) factor cancels from normalized labelled probabilities but matters when defining thermodynamic partition functions.
reconstruction: The Gaussian factor and normalization qualification are supplied.
fate: The reduction is in \citet[Lecture I]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established exact factorization.

title: A hard-core lattice gas
notes: States are distinct sites of a cubic lattice; \(U(x)\) is even, without requiring spherical symmetry.
statement: On a finite \(\Omega\subset\mathbb Z^d\), configurations are \(N\)-element subsets, or labelled distinct tuples with the corresponding symmetry factor. An even pair interaction \(U(z)=U(-z)\) defines \(W_N=\sum_{i\ne j}U(x_i-x_j)\). Lattice symmetry does not imply rotational invariance.
fate: This recurs from 1964-3.1; see \citet[Lecture I]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Repulsion, decay, and the Lennard--Jones example
notes: \(U(r)=a r^{-12}-b r^{-6}\), \(a,b>0\), illustrates short-range repulsion and decay; finite-range and hard-core versions are also drawn.
statement: For rigorous limits one needs quantitative assumptions, for example stability \(W_N\geq-BN\) and integrable tails or \(\int|e^{-\beta\phi(x)}-1|\,dx<\infty\). In physical dimension three the Lennard--Jones form has the appropriate repulsive core and integrable far tail. Mere growth at zero and decay at infinity, without rates or stability, are insufficient.
reconstruction: The precise stability and regularity assumptions are editorial additions.
fate: The stability issue was treated before this lecture by \citet{fisherruelle1966stability}; later density-expansion hypotheses are explicit in \citet[\S2]{kunatsagkarogiannis2018density}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established framework. The aside that physicists use only this potential is not a mathematical theorem.

title: Thermodynamic scaling and vessel regularity
notes: \(\Omega_N\) fills space, \(|\Omega_N|/N\to v\), and the vessel shape is usually immaterial.
statement: Take \(N\to\infty\), \(|\Omega_N|\to\infty\), \(N/|\Omega_N|\to\rho=1/v\in(0,\infty)\), with a van Hove exhaustion: for each fixed \(a>0\), the volume of the \(a\)-boundary strip is \(o(|\Omega_N|)\). Shape-independent limits require hypotheses on the interaction and on the quantity being limited.
reconstruction: The van Hove condition replaces an unrestricted exhaustion.
fate: This continues 1964-3.2; the boundary-strip condition is explicit in \citet[Lecture III, \S4, p.~164]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard scaling, not a theorem that every correlation limit is unique at every density.

title: The finite canonical Gibbs law
notes: \(p(a)=Q^{-1}e^{-\beta H(a)}\), \(Q=\int e^{-\beta H}\), is postulated in equilibrium; for a lattice replace density by probabilities.
statement: Given a reference measure and \(0<Q<\infty\), the canonical law at fixed \(N,\Omega,\beta>0\) has that density. Stationarity alone does not characterize it: many functions of the energy yield invariant laws for Hamiltonian dynamics.
reconstruction: Normalization and the logical status of the postulate are supplied.
fate: The canonical ensemble is introduced in \citet[Lecture I]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established equilibrium model; the Gibbs form is an assumption here, not deduced merely from time-independence.

title: Factorial correlation densities
notes: \(\tau_k=(N!/(N-k)!)p(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\), where \(p\) is a marginal density.
statement: For a symmetric labelled \(N\)-particle density, \(r_k=(N)_kp_k\), \((N)_k=N(N-1)\cdots(N-k+1)\). It represents ordered distinct particle tuples: \(\mathbb E\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_k\ {\rm distinct}}h(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_k})=\int h r_k\), whenever the integral is meaningful.
reconstruction: We use \(r_k\) as a typographically unambiguous synonym for the notebook’s \(\tau_k\).
fate: The factorial convention is explicit in \citet[Lecture III, \S1]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard. These densities are not normalized probability densities.

title: Expectations of summatory observables
notes: First- and second-order summatory functions have means \(\int f\tau_1\) and \(\iint f\tau_2\).
statement: For an integrable test function, \(\mathbb E\sum_if(x_i)=\int_\Omega f(x)r_1(x)\,dx\). For an integrable symmetric pair kernel, \(\mathbb E\sum_{i\ne j}h(x_i,x_j)=\int_{\Omega^2}h(x,y)r_2(x,y)\,dx\,dy\); no additional factor \(1/2\) occurs.
fate: These identities are used in \citet[Lecture III, \S1 and \S4]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: exact consequences of the definition.

title: Local mean particle density
notes: For the particle count \(n_C\), \(\mathbb E n_C=\int_C\tau_1\); small regions identify \(\tau_1\) as local mean density.
statement: For measurable \(C\subset\Omega\), \(\mathbb E n_C=\int_Cr_1\). If \(r_1\) is locally integrable, averages over shrinking balls converge to \(r_1(x)\) at its Lebesgue points; if it is continuous, this holds at every interior point.
reconstruction: Lebesgue points specify the sense of the limiting density.
fate: The interpretation is given in \citet[Lecture III, \S1]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established, with the usual differentiation qualifications.

title: Probability of exactly one point in a small region
notes: \(P(n_{\Delta C}=1)=\tau_1(x_0)\Delta C+o(\Delta C)\).
statement: For shrinking neighbourhoods \(C\) of \(x_0\), continuity of \(r_1\) there and a locally bounded \(r_2\) imply \(P(n_C=1)=r_1(x_0)|C|+o(|C|)\). Indeed \(0\leq\mathbb E n_C-P(n_C=1)\leq\mathbb E[n_C(n_C-1)]=\int_{C^2}r_2=O(|C|^2)\).
reconstruction: The explicit factorial-moment estimate is supplied.
fate: The local interpretation occurs in \citet[Lecture III, \S1]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct with control of multiple occupancy; hard cores make that control immediate in sufficiently small cells.

title: Two-cell probabilities and the second correlation density
notes: \(\tau(x_1,x_2)\Delta x_1\Delta x_2\) is the probability of one particle in each of two small cells.
statement: For disjoint shrinking cells \(C_1,C_2\) around distinct points, continuous \(r_2\) and locally bounded \(r_3,r_4\) yield \(P(n_{C_1}=n_{C_2}=1)=r_2(x_1,x_2)|C_1||C_2|+o(|C_1||C_2|)\). The exact identity without small-cell qualification is \(\mathbb E(n_{C_1}n_{C_2})=\int_{C_1\times C_2}r_2\).
reconstruction: Disjointness and multiple-occupancy bounds are supplied.
fate: Factorial interpretation: \citet[Lecture III, \S1]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct as a leading-order interpretation, not an exact finite-cell probability.

title: Bulk-correlation hypotheses with an unspecified exceptional set
notes: Hypotheses 1--5 assert limiting \(\bar\tau_k\), a boundary-distance error, translation invariance, continuity away from exceptional parameters, and boundedness. The effective \(v_N\) may depend on \(k\).
statement: For a specified stable finite-range continuum pair potential and fixed \((\rho,\beta)\), ask for a canonical bulk limit \(r_{k,N}\to r_k\), independent of a regular vessel exhaustion, and quantitative boundary/mixing estimates strong enough to integrate products of local observables. The dilute regime supplies such results in explicit ranges; the notebook proposes an extension through thermodynamic regimes, without specifying the exceptional set.
reconstruction: The conditional moment implication is audited separately under item 1966-100.11. Its completed proof is not presented as an open-problem advance. The broader programme cannot be converted into a precise C question by silently defining its exceptional set.
fate: The 1968 account retains hypotheses and asks for precise inequalities \citep[Lecture III, \S3 and Problem 3, p.~164]{minlos1968lectures}. Dilute canonical results appear in \citet[Theorem 2.5 and Corollary 2.6]{pulvirentitsagkarogiannis2015finite} and \citet[Theorems 2.1,2.7]{kunatsagkarogiannis2018density}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the programme has rigorous dilute-regime realizations, but no precise all-density residual conjecture is certified by this source. The exceptional set and admissible phase selection are unspecified. F records this failure of exact formulation, not a failure to recognize the subject.

title: An order-dependent effective specific volume
notes: For every \(\tau_k\) there is \(v_N\), depending on the vessel and \(k\), that improves the boundary approximation; \(v_N\to v\).
statement: In the ideal canonical gas of volume \(V\), \(r_{k,N}=(N)_k/V^k\). The infinite-volume ideal density is \(\rho^k\). For each fixed \(k\leq N\), choosing \(\rho_{N,k}=(N)_k^{1/k}/V\), equivalently \(v_{N,k}=V/(N)_k^{1/k}\), matches that order exactly and \(v_{N,k}\to v\). A single \(\rho_N\) cannot match both orders 1 and 2.
reconstruction: \ours\ The explicit \(k\)-dependent formula is calculated here and checked by the supplied code. It verifies only the ideal gas, not interacting boundary rates.
fate: The canonical adjustment is discussed in \citet[Lecture III, \S3, p.~161]{minlos1968lectures}; the exact ideal-gas calculation is elementary.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the notebook’s \(k\)-dependent quantifier passes the ideal-gas test. The stronger common-parameter version would fail.

title: The exponential wall-rate claim and its missing regime
notes: For compactly supported potentials the decay function is indicated as \(e^{-\lambda r}\). Continuity may fail at exceptional \((v,\beta)\).
statement: The displayed \(\gamma\) controls error by distance to the vessel wall, after the order-dependent parameter adjustment. This is distinct from spatial decay between two particle clusters. A precise theorem would specify the potential, thermodynamic regime, boundary conditions, and adjustment before asserting an exponential wall estimate. The notes explicitly allow exceptional parameters and failure of the rate at some volumes per particle.
reconstruction: The canonical correction in the development concerns unadjusted pair covariance. The ideal gas actually supports the separate k-dependent wall-parameter adjustment, so that calculation does not refute this source claim.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2.5, Corollary 2.6]{pulvirentitsagkarogiannis2015finite} gives a related dilute two-point estimate with a finite-volume term; it is not an exact match to this adjusted wall-error assertion.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: no exact theorem with the notebook’s undeclared regime was identified. Its qualified claim is not refuted by imposing a universal quantifier it never states.

title: Translation invariance, continuity, and the density parameter
notes: Translation invariance gives \(\bar\tau_1=\rho\). The notes say the hypotheses are proved for small \(v\) and \(\beta\), crediting Ruelle.
statement: A translation-invariant state has a constant one-point density; identifying it with the imposed canonical density additionally uses bulk convergence without loss of mass. The perturbative gas regime is small density/activity, hence large specific volume \(v=1/\rho\), not small \(v\). Within a convergent expansion, correlations depend analytically on the appropriate parameter.
reconstruction: The relation \(v=1/\rho\) is already explicit on P000155 and determines the correction.
fate: Ruelle’s gas-phase results appeared in 1963--1964 \citep{ruelle1963correlation,ruelle1964cluster}; canonical density expansions are made precise by \citet[Theorem 2.7]{kunatsagkarogiannis2018density}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the qualitative gas-phase conclusion is established; the source’s volume/density wording is inverted.

title: Can arbitrary initial distributions lead to Gibbs laws?
notes: Gelfand suggests that any distribution might approach Gibbs as particle number increases; Arnold objects that an ergodic hypothesis is missing.
statement: Without a rule associating initial laws and dynamics for different \(N\), this is not one convergence theorem. Invariance or ergodicity on an energy surface concerns a microcanonical measure, whereas a canonical law mixes energy levels. Deterministic Hamiltonian evolution preserves energy and cannot send every initial energy distribution to one prescribed canonical distribution.
fate: The ensemble distinction is treated in \citet[Lecture II]{minlos1968lectures}; no exact publication is identified for this exchange.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the unrestricted universality suggestion fails; no definite residual conjecture is recoverable.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand; intervention by V. I. Arnold

title: Representativity is concentration of a normalized sequence
notes: \(P(|F-\langle F\rangle|>\epsilon)\to0\); the notes immediately call this imprecise because there is no one function \(F\).
statement: For an extensive observable \(F_N\), the intended property is \((F_N-\mathbb EF_N)/N\to0\) in probability. If \(\mathbb EF_N/N\to m\), this gives \(F_N/N\to m\). Unnormalized fluctuations need not converge to zero.
reconstruction: The triangular sequence of observables and probability laws is made explicit.
fate: The normalization is explicit in \citet[Lecture III, \S4]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established definition; the notebook itself flags the shorthand.

title: An integrable pair observable
notes: \(F_N=\sum_{i\ne j}f(x_i-x_j)\), with one fixed \(f\) and \(\int|f|<\infty\).
statement: Use a real even measurable \(f\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)\) and ordered pairs. A uniform bound \(r_{2,N}\leq C_2\) implies \(\mathbb E|F_N|\leq C_2|\Omega_N|\|f\|_1\). It does not imply a finite second moment. The symmetry condition is inherited from the preceding lecture.
reconstruction: Explicit evenness and the moment distinction are supplied.
fate: The same integrability assumption is (3.24) in \citet[Lecture III, \S4]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the expectation is controlled; variance needs additional short-distance integrability.

title: The mean per particle has a correlation-integral limit
notes: \(\langle F_N\rangle=|\Omega_N|\int\bar\tau_2(\xi)f(\xi)\,d\xi+o(|\Omega_N|)\), hence the mean per particle tends to \(v\) times that integral.
statement: A sufficient precise hypothesis is \(r_{2,N}\leq C_2\) and almost-everywhere convergence of \(A_N(z)=|\Omega_N|^{-1}\int\mathbf1_{\Omega_N}(x)\mathbf1_{\Omega_N}(x-z)r_{2,N}(x,x-z)\,dx\) to a bulk function \(R(z)\). Then dominated convergence gives \(\mathbb EF_N/|\Omega_N|\to\int fR\), and \(\mathbb EF_N/N\to v\int fR\) if \(|\Omega_N|/N\to v\). Pointwise convergence near a fixed origin alone is insufficient.
reconstruction: Uniform integrability and the vessel condition are supplied; the final subscript must remain 2.
fate: The calculation is published in \citet[Lecture III, \S4, pp.~162--163]{minlos1968lectures}, from the 1965/1966 lectures.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: valid under the stated uniform bulk hypotheses.

title: The multiplicative cluster property
notes: \(|\bar\tau_{k+s}-\bar\tau_k\bar\tau_s|\leq C_{k,s}\gamma(\min|x_i-y_j|)\) is said to follow, with difficulty, from preceding hypotheses.
statement: This is a mixing property of the limiting state and requires more than existence, boundedness, translation invariance and continuity of correlations. For example a stationary mixture of Poisson processes of two distinct intensities has bounded factorial densities of each order but a nonzero, distance-independent two-point connected correlation.
reconstruction: \ours\ If the random intensity is \(Z\in\{a,b\}\), \(r_k=\mathbb EZ^k\), and \(r_2-r_1^2=\operatorname{Var}Z>0\). This example refutes the logical implication between qualitative correlation properties; it is not claimed to be a canonical limit for the notebook’s fixed potential.
fate: The gas-phase cluster theorem predates the talk \citep{ruelle1964cluster}. The general inference is not supplied by \citet[Lecture III, \S3]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in suitable pure/uniqueness regimes; false as an automatic consequence of the qualitative properties listed.

title: The claimed linear variance and its integrability gap
notes: \(DF_N\sim dN\), so \(D(F_N/N)\sim d/N\) and Chebyshev gives representativity.
statement: With \(f\in L^1\cap L^2\), bounded second and third factorial densities, and an integrable finite-volume two-pair connected bound allowing an \(O(V^{-1})\) canonical term, one obtains \(\operatorname{Var}F_N=O(V)=O(N)\). These assumptions alone do not give a positive asymptotic coefficient. With only \(L^1\), variance can be infinite; concentration can nevertheless follow by truncation under the same correlation bounds.
reconstruction: \ours\ The repair, sharp distinction of moments, and truncation implication are proved in the development. They clarify the bounded implication within GP-1966-09, rather than solve its general thermodynamic part.
fate: The 1968 proof adds integrable decay and a van Hove condition in its p.~164 remark \citep[Lecture III, \S4]{minlos1968lectures}, but still displays \(f^2\) after assuming only (3.24).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the notebook’s stated assumptions do not prove the variance asymptotic. The chapter supplies a complete conditional repair and a counterexample, without claiming novelty for the probabilistic method.

title: The exact ordered-pair square expansion
notes: \(F_N^2=2\sum_{i\ne j}f_{ij}^2+4\sum_{i,j,k\ {\rm distinct}}f_{ij}f_{kj}+\sum_{i,j,k,s\ {\rm distinct}}f_{ij}f_{ks}\).
statement: For \(f_{ij}=f_{ji}\), this identity partitions two ordered pairs by whether their union has two, three, or four labels. Integration gives coefficients 2, 4, and 1 against \(r_2,r_3,r_4\), respectively. All three sums are over ordered distinct tuples as displayed.
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The evenness requirement is explicit; the exact combinatorial verification is supplied with its output.
fate: The same combinatorial calculation occurs in \citet[Lecture III, \S4, p.~163]{minlos1968lectures}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: exact. The supplied code checks the identity on exhaustive small labelled configurations independently of the proof.

title: Finite abelianization of the lattice
notes: If the simple real or \(p\)-adic group \(G\) contains \(\mathrm{SL}(3,P)\), and \(\Gamma\) is discrete with finite-volume quotient, then \(\Gamma/[\Gamma,\Gamma]\) is finite.
statement: Let \(K\) be a nondiscrete locally compact field. Every lattice in \(\mathrm{SL}_3(K)\) has finite abelianization. The same conclusion holds for a locally compact group \(G\) with property \(T\), including the simple algebraic groups covered by Kazhdan’s Theorem 6. In that extension the algebraic subgroup and compact-generation hypotheses of that theorem must be retained.
reconstruction: The explicit \(\mathrm{SL}_3(K)\) case is exact. The larger-group wording is restricted to the published theorem rather than extrapolated from the notebook’s abbreviation.
fate: \citet[Theorems 1, 3, 5--6]{kazhdan1967dual}; received 10 October 1966, published 1967.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. Containing an arbitrary property-\(T\) subgroup, without the ambient hypotheses, does not transfer property \(T\) to every group.

title: Finite generation of the lattice
notes: \(\Gamma\) has finitely many generators, even extractable from any generating set.
statement: A countable discrete group with property \(T\) is finitely generated; hence the lattices of the preceding item are finitely generated. Any generating set of a finitely generated group contains a finite generating subset, since finitely many fixed generators use only finitely many words in that set.
reconstruction: The parenthetical strengthening is the elementary finite-word argument, not a stronger finiteness property.
fate: \citet[Theorems 2--3]{kazhdan1967dual}, announced here in September 1966 and printed in 1967.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. Finite presentation is a separate assertion and is not stated in these notes.

title: Isolation of the trivial unitary representation
notes: The proof uses \ru{изолированность единичного представления}, isolation of the trivial representation.
statement: For a locally compact group, property \(T\) means that every unitary representation with almost invariant unit vectors has a nonzero invariant vector. Equivalently, the trivial representation is isolated in the appropriate unitary-dual topology. Kazhdan proves this for \(\mathrm{SL}_3(K)\) and transfers it to finite-covolume closed subgroups.
reconstruction: Almost invariant vectors give an explicit modern formulation of the isolated-representation shorthand.
fate: \citet[\S1 and Theorems 3, 5]{kazhdan1967dual}. The terminology and mechanism occur in the original 1967 paper.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the notes record the central innovation, not merely its later name.

title: A rational-group representation fragment
notes: An algebraic group over \(\mathbb Q\) containing \(\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb Q)\) is followed only by \ru{что-то о представлениях}, something about representations.
statement: No asserted property of representations, topology on \(G(\mathbb Q)\), or class of representations survives. Neither a local-field property-\(T\) theorem nor an automorphic theorem can be inferred from this sentence.
fate: The nearby results match \citet{kazhdan1967dual}; the rational-group fragment has no exact statement to match.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: unidentified as a mathematical assertion, even though its subject is clear.

title: Monotonicity of zero spacing and its alleged converse
notes: Under the label Sturm (1836), increasing \(f\) in \(y^{\prime\prime}+fy=0\) makes consecutive zeros closer, “and conversely.”
statement: For a continuous increasing coefficient on an oscillatory interval, Sturm comparison gives nonincreasing consecutive zero gaps, with strictness under an appropriate strict comparison. Decreasing gaps of one solution do not conversely force its coefficient to be increasing.
reconstruction: \ours\ For \(x>1\), put \(y=x^{-1/2}e^{\epsilon\cos(2x^2)}\sin(x^2)\), \(\epsilon=1/100\). Its zeros \(\sqrt{k\pi}\) have strictly decreasing gaps. Direct differentiation gives \(f=x^2[4+16\epsilon+32\epsilon\cos(2x^2)-16\epsilon^2\sin^2(2x^2)]-3/(4x^2)\). This is smooth and positive on \((1,\infty)\), but \(f^{\prime}<0\) at all sufficiently large points with \(2x^2=\pi/2+2k\pi\). Thus even positive oscillatory coefficients do not satisfy the proposed converse. The identity is checked symbolically in the supplied code.
fate: The comparison-theory setting precedes the talk and is the starting point of \citet[Introduction]{lorchszego1963higher}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the forward comparison is standard; the unrestricted converse is false.

title: Higher monotonicity needs a nondegeneracy condition
notes: The assumptions are \((-1)^jf^{(j+1)}\geq0\), \(j=1,\ldots,N\), and \(f(\infty)>0\); the conclusion is \((-1)^n\Delta^{n+1}x_k>0\).
statement: The written statement fails for \(f\equiv1\), whose zero gaps are constant. A checked sufficient theorem is formulated through independent real solutions \(y_1,y_2\) and \(p=y_1^2+y_2^2\): if \(p>0\), \(-p^{\prime}>0\), and \((-1)^jp^{(j)}\geq0\) for \(2\leq j\leq N\), with the derivatives continuous up to order \(N-1\) and the last derivative existing on the interval, then the alternating finite differences of zero gaps are strictly positive through the stated orders wherever the zeros exist.
reconstruction: \ours\ The constant-coefficient counterexample also survives adding the missing \(j=0\) weak inequality. Accordingly no silent change of an index repairs strictness.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2.1]{lorchszego1963higher} has the strict phase-amplitude conditions; \citet[Theorem, pp.~447--448]{muldoon1968extension} weakens the higher ones while retaining \(-p^{\prime}>0\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the theorem family is established, but the exact recorded coefficient-only formulation is false. The later phase-amplitude theorem is a partial, explicitly different match.

title: The Bessel and Airy examples
notes: Bessel functions with \(\nu>1/2\), Airy functions, and others are listed as examples.
statement: Writing \(u(x)=\sqrt{x}\,J_\nu(x)\) puts the Bessel equation in normal form \(u^{\prime\prime}+[1-(\nu^2-1/4)x^{-2}]u=0\). The oscillatory Airy equation is \(u^{\prime\prime}+xu=0\), for example \(u=\operatorname{Ai}(-x)\). Normal-form dependent variables and the oscillatory branch must be specified before importing zero or wave-integral assertions.
reconstruction: The normalizing factor and the sign of the Airy argument are supplied.
fate: These special-function applications belong to \citet[applications]{lorchszego1963higher}; the transformed equations identify the notebook’s examples.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established examples. A statement about wave areas of \(J_\nu\) itself is not identical to one about \(\sqrt{x}J_\nu\).

title: Higher monotonicity of wave integrals
notes: For consecutive zeros, \(M_k=\int_{x_k}^{x_{k+1}}|y|^\lambda\,dx\), \(\lambda>-1\), has the same property; \(\lambda=0\) gives gaps and \(\lambda=1\) areas.
statement: Under the phase-amplitude hypotheses in item 1966-102.2, \((-1)^n\Delta^nM_k>0\) for \(0\leq n\leq N\), whenever all required consecutive zeros lie in the interval. Nontrivial solutions have simple zeros, and \(\lambda>-1\) is the exact local integrability condition there.
reconstruction: The range of differences is explicitly limited by the available zeros.
fate: \citet[Theorem 2.1]{lorchszego1963higher}; the weakened hypotheses and unchanged conclusion are in \citet[Theorem]{muldoon1968extension}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the stated hypotheses; the finite-difference order for gaps is one higher because \(M_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) when \(\lambda=0\).

title: The divergent endpoint and reciprocal derivatives
notes: Gelfand’s \(\lambda=-1\) remark contains \(1/y^{\prime}(x_k)\) and an unresolved abbreviation; it is not a complete limiting formula.
statement: The ordinary integral at \(\lambda=-1\) diverges at every simple endpoint zero. A precise nearby identity, not asserted to be the intended one, is \(\lim_{\lambda\downarrow-1}(\lambda+1)\int_a^b|y(x)|^\lambda dx=|y^{\prime}(a)|^{-1}+|y^{\prime}(b)|^{-1}\) for consecutive simple zeros of a \(C^1\) function with no zero inside.
reconstruction: \ours\ Near \(a\), for \(0<\delta<|y^{\prime}(a)|\), \((|y^{\prime}(a)|-\delta)(x-a)\leq|y(x)|\leq(|y^{\prime}(a)|+\delta)(x-a)\). Integrating these bounds with \(-1<\lambda<0\), multiplying by \(\lambda+1\), taking the limit and then \(\delta\downarrow0\) gives the first reciprocal. Repeat at \(b\); on the remaining compact interval the scaled integral tends to zero. The sine example is independently checked with the beta-integral formula.
fate: The integral theorem in \citet{lorchszego1963higher} assumes \(\lambda>-1\); no checked source identifies the exact endpoint remark.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal ordinary integral is divergent; the intended regularization or signed difference remains unidentified.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Equivariant K-theory as a contravariant ring functor
notes: For compact \(G\), equivariant bundles and formal differences define \(K_G(X)\); the functor is contravariant and receives \(R(G)\) from \(X\to*\).
statement: For a compact Lie group and compact \(G\)-space in the finite \(G\)-CW setting, complex equivariant vector bundles form the Grothendieck ring \(K_G^0(X)\). Pullback gives contravariance, and \(K_G^0(*)=R(G)\) acts by tensoring with representation bundles.
reconstruction: Finite \(G\)-CW hypotheses align the next completion statement with its checked classical scope.
fate: The definitions precede this reprise; see \citet[Introduction]{atiyahsegal1969completion} and the earlier occurrences 1966-97.1 and 1966-98.4.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard. Being an \(R(G)\)-algebra does not require the structural homomorphism to be injective.

title: The Borel construction is not the ordinary orbit space
notes: \(X_G=E\times_GX\) is called a generalization of the classifying space; for a point it is \(BG\). The accompanying phrase says the orbits are contracted to points.
statement: For a contractible free \(G\)-space \(EG\), the diagonal quotient \(EG\times_GX\) is the homotopy quotient and is a bundle over \(BG\) with fibre \(X\). Only for free suitable actions is it homotopy equivalent to \(X/G\). For trivial actions it is \(BG\times X\).
reconstruction: The distinction between homotopy and ordinary quotient is made explicit.
fate: This is the construction used by \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}; it repeats item 1966-98.5.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard. The orbit phrase must refer to the diagonal action, not the loss of all isotropy information from \(X\).

title: The approximate identification means I-adic completion
notes: \(K_G(X)\) approximately coincides with \(K(X_G)\).
statement: For a finite \(G\)-CW complex and compact Lie \(G\), the comparison identifies the augmentation-ideal completion of \(K_G^*(X)\) with \(K^*(EG\times_GX)\), interpreted through the skeletal inverse system. It is generally not an isomorphism from the uncompleted ring.
reconstruction: The ideal, completion, grading, and finiteness assumptions are supplied.
fate: \citet{atiyahsegal1969completion}, printed 1969, supplies the general completion theorem. Atiyah’s earlier special cases and Bernstein’s exposition account for the result circulating before this occurrence.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated finite setting; this is the same theorem family as item 1966-98.6.

title: Twisting a vertical elliptic family
notes: For a fibration \(Y\to X\) with compact manifold fibre \(M_x\), a family \(D_x\) acts between restrictions of two bundles; twisting by a bundle \(V\) on \(Y\) gives an elliptic family.
statement: Let \(p:Y\to X\) be a smooth fibre bundle with closed fibres and compact base, and let \(D\) be a continuous family of vertical elliptic differential operators between complex vector bundles. A chosen connection defines a twist \(D\otimes V\) with symbol \(\sigma(D)\otimes1_V\); its analytic index defines an additive homomorphism \(p_!^D:K^0(Y)\to K^0(X)\).
reconstruction: Closed fibres, compact base, operator continuity, and a connection are supplied. The symbol determines the index.
fate: The family-index construction was discussed in Atiyah’s 1966 congress lecture, printed in 1968, and fully developed in \citet[\S2, Proposition 2.2 and Definition 2.3]{atiyahsinger1971families}; see \citet{atiyah1968global}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. Independence of auxiliary choices is an index assertion, not the claim that twisting a differential operator is connection-free.

title: The direct image obeys the projection formula
notes: The reverse map is required to be a map of \(K(X)\)-modules; the de Rham complex is mentioned as an example.
statement: For the family index, \(p_!^D(p^*a\cdot b)=a\cdot p_!^D(b)\). A left inverse to \(p^*\) follows only if \(p_!^D(1)=1\). A de Rham family has fibrewise numerical index \(\chi(M)\), which need not equal one; the Dolbeault operator on the flag fibre used in the completion argument has index one.
reconstruction: The condition on the index of 1 is the missing algebraic step that connects this construction to the preceding completion argument.
fate: The family-index framework is in \citet[\S2, Proposition 2.2 and Definition 2.3]{atiyahsinger1971families}; Atiyah discusses the flag-manifold direct image in \citet{atiyah1988commentary}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. An arbitrary elliptic family is not automatically a retraction of pullback.

title: Kernels and cokernels need not form vector bundles
notes: Finite-dimensional kernels and cokernels are subtracted to obtain an element of K-theory; after a projected deformation the kernel dimension is said to be locally constant.
statement: A norm-continuous family of Fredholm operators has locally constant numerical index but need not have locally constant kernel or cokernel dimension. For \(A_t:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\), \(A_tz=tz\), both dimensions jump at \(t=0\). Thus the virtual index requires stabilization or local patching.
reconstruction: \ours\ The one-dimensional family is a direct counterexample to the unstabilized bundle claim: its kernel is zero for \(t\ne0\) and \(\mathbb C\) at zero.
fate: This distinction underlies the family construction of \citet[\S2, Proposition 2.2 and Definition 2.3]{atiyahsinger1971families}; it also explains the Fredholm discussion in \citet{atiyah1968global}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The abbreviated difference is valid only after the required index-bundle construction.

title: A rigorous finite-dimensional stabilization
notes: A map \(X\to F(H,H)\) is modified through \(A_x(1-t)+tA_xP_V\), where the projection’s precise definition is abbreviated.
statement: For a compact Hausdorff base \(X\), complex Hilbert spaces \(H_0,H_1\), and norm-continuous Fredholm family \(A_x:H_0\to H_1\), choose a finite-dimensional \(V\subset H_1\) with \(\operatorname{im}A_x+V=H_1\) for every \(x\). The augmented operators \(B_x:H_0\oplus V\to H_1\), \(B_x(u,v)=A_xu+v\), are surjective and their kernels form a finite-rank vector bundle. Define \(\operatorname{Ind}(A)=[\ker B]-[X\times V]\).
reconstruction: \ours\ For each \(x\), a complement to the range gives a surjective augmentation on a neighbourhood; a finite cover supplies a common \(V\). Locally a continuous right inverse exists by the Neumann-series argument, so the kernels form a bundle. Enlarging \(V\) to \(W\) yields \(0\to\ker B_V\to\ker B_W\to X\times(W/V)\to0\), preserving the virtual class. A common enlargement compares any two choices. Apply the same argument over compact \(X\times[0,1]\) for homotopy invariance.
fate: This is the standard family-index construction, contemporary with the 1966 lecture and recorded in \citet[\S2, Proposition 2.2 and Definition 2.3]{atiyahsinger1971families}. The specific projected formula in the notebook is not asserted to be an exact transcription of that argument.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established. The resulting class is independent of the auxiliary finite-dimensional subspace and homotopy invariant.
